item.description: Dr. Xiaochen Y Zheng I - left one on the picture - am a cognitive neuroscientist who’s always excited about the cognitive control processes in the brain, especially how they are shared between language and other cognitive systems. In 2024 Fall, I joined the Department of Cognitive Psychology in Leiden University, thanks to a Veni grant from the Dutch Research Council. With this grant, I explore how cognitive control regulates multiple streams of information in working memory during context-dependent speech.

Contact me I am usually quite reachable by email, zhengxiaochen dot psy at gmail dot com Cannot risk any auto-reply? Then check the homepage and hope you will figure out how to find me faster. Good luck!!

News New Dr. and proud (first-time!) supervisor 18th September 2026 Our very own Elena Mainetto successfully defended her PhD thesis, “The Role of Dopamine in Word Meaning Inference,” at Radboud University, Donders Institute for Brain, Cognition, and Behaviour. 🎓 Elena’s work advanced our understanding of how dopamine shapes the neural processes behind inferring and representing word meaning during language processing - tying together psycholinguistics, psychopharmacology, functional MRI, and computational modelling.

Projects The age of information overload: how do we control what we say? This research is funded by a Veni grant (€320,000) from the Dutch Research Council (NWO). We have all been there: you are in the middle of saying something, and suddenly a notification pops up on your phone. Your attention shifts momentarily and you lose track of what you were going to say.
